purpose: Ground the Device Worker so it can answer the questions a user actually asks about their laptop. Section 4.7 makes device_model a required filter on every query against these.

notes.user_agent: dl.dell.com and delltechnologies.com return 403 to a default user-agent. The fetch script sends a browser one.
notes.wayback: Documents with a wayback block were removed from the vendor's live site. The archive serves the vendor's original bytes through the id_ raw form — https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<original-url>. Omitting id_ returns an archive-wrapped HTML page that will still start with %PDF-less markup.
notes.portals: Dell and Apple support portals are JavaScript-rendered and bot-protected. No Dell topicspdf PDF has ever existed for the 2024 Latitude 5550, 2024 Latitude 7350 or Precision 3460 — checked against 4,353 archived dl.dell.com/topicspdf URLs.

documents.warning: A three-column comparison of the Latitude 5350, 5450 and 5550. Extraction keeps the row labels and loses the column headers, so a MEMORY OPTIONS or STORAGE OPTIONS chunk contains all three models' values with nothing marking which is which — the 5350's onboard LPDDR5 sits directly above the 5550's upgradeable DDR5. Layout-aware extraction is what recovers the association. Dell removed this from its live site; the archive is now the only source, and no Dell PDF has ever carried Latitude 5550 troubleshooting procedures.

apple_support_articles.note: Apple publishes no service manual PDF and its repair manual is HTML only, so the MacBook Pro model file carries this index instead. These are POINTERS, not quotations — the authoritative text lives at each URL. Every URL was opened and confirmed to return the article it claims; one candidate (mchlp2582) resolved to the generic Mac User Guide landing page and was dropped. Note that support.apple.com is unreachable by curl from some networks, so these are not machine-verifiable by the fetch script.
